scenes.script_line: A new story only lasts if you believe it. And belief needs reasons. Your old story had years of reasons behind it, some true and many not. Your new story needs reasons too. So in step eight, you'll make the case for why your new story is true, and why it fits. There are two parts. Part A, on page seventeen, is about benefit. You're writing how specifically the new story supports what matters most to you from step one. scenes.script_line: Part B, on page eighteen, is about alignment. You're writing why the new story is more aligned with who you truly are. Start with, "The new story is more aligned with who I truly am because…" Think back to your core, from the beginning of this workshop. The old story was shaped by fear and outside voices. The new story comes from what's actually true about you. Sam wrote, "The new story is more aligned with who I truly am because people already trust my judgement, and because I care more about the team than about looking perfect."

scenes.script_line: Notice that Sam isn't inventing anything. Sam is recognising what was already there. Here's how the workbook puts it. "I am someone committed to moving forward, and this story supports me in that pursuit, because it is more aligned with who I really am." Then anchor your new story in at least two strong reasons or pieces of evidence that confirm it's true. These might be facts from your life, feedback you've received, or principles you deeply trust.

shots.text: person reading a line back and nodding slightly

colleague recalling a piece of feedback, speaking warmly

scenes.script_line: Why does this matter? Because evidence is stronger than encouragement. Anyone can repeat a positive sentence. But a story backed by real reasons is very hard to argue with, even on a difficult day. When your mind tries to slip back into the old story, and at times it will, these anchors are what hold you steady.

shots.text: person sitting with a steady, settled expression under pressure
close-up of a hand touching a written anchor statement on a page
person taking a breath, holding steady on a hard day

scenes.script_line: Think of it like building a case. Part A shows the new story is good for you. Part B shows the new story is true of you. Together, they make it very hard for the old story to come back. Your facilitator will now guide you through both parts.
